chunks: Al-Ḥakam ibn Miskīn narrated from Qutaybah ibn al-Aʿshā, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, “I recite the Qur’an, and a gift is presented to me, so may I accept it?” He said: “No.”
I said, “If I did not stipulate it as a condition?” He said, “Tell me: if you had not recited it, would he have given you a gift?”
He said: I replied, “No.” He said: “Then do not accept it.”

key_terms.أَقْرَأُ: I recite; specifically, the act of reciting the Qur’an
key_terms.أُشَارِطْهُ: I stipulate it as a condition beforehand
key_terms.الْقُرْآنَ: the Qur’an, whose recitation is the subject of the ruling
key_terms.الْهَدِيَّةُ: a gift offered to the reciter
key_terms.فَلَا تَقْبَلْهُ: then do not accept it; the Imam’s ruling

ai.seo_question: Can someone accept gifts given in return for reciting the Qur’an if no condition was set beforehand?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning accepting gifts given because of Qur’an recitation. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام teaches that if the gift is only being given due to the recitation, it should not be accepted, even if no explicit condition was stated.
